title: Day 2 — Ambiguous Scoping
prompt: Our label printer prints a fixed number of characters per line. Given a piece of text and a width, return how many lines you'd need to write it (and the wrapped lines). That's the whole ticket — go.

clarifications.answer: Words are whitespace-separated; runs of spaces collapse and leading/trailing whitespace is ignored.
A word longer than the width is NOT split — it overflows onto its own line.
A newline already in the text is a HARD break — each newline-delimited segment wraps independently.
Empty or whitespace-only text needs 0 lines (returns []).
width <= 0 is invalid and raises ValueError.
Greedy word wrap: pack words joined by single spaces until the next won't fit, then start a new line.

hints: Resist coding — first list every decision the one-sentence ask left open (word breaks, over-long words, newlines, empty, width<=0).
Implement wrap_lines first; line_count is just len(wrap_lines(text, width)).
Split on '\n' for hard breaks, then greedily pack each segment's words at the width; an over-long word gets its own line.
